text: I work on iron and zinc fortification of oat and pea drinks, and most of what goes wrong is binding: phytate, polyphenols, the proteins themselves. I keep pulling out a printed periodic table to compare electronegativity between the minerals and the atoms they end up bound to (O, N, S, P). could you make me a periodic table page where each element's box is coloured by its electronegativity (pauling) and also has a small bar in the box, so I can read the trend across a row without trusting the colour alone? hover should give me the number. only need H through Xe, nothing heavier matters in food. He Ne and Ar have no pauling value so leave them blank, don't show 0

nice. can I click an element to pin it in a panel on the right so it stays there while I hover around? I want to pin several (Fe Zn Ca Mg Cu, plus O and S) and see them in a small table side by side. outline the pinned ones on the table too. and if I pin two tell me the electronegativity difference, thats what I actually use for how ionic the bond is
add a switch so the colours and bars can show atomic radius or first ionization energy instead. the pinned table should keep all three columns whichever one is on

there's no key so I can't tell what dark blue means. put a scale under the table with min, max and units, and show where the element I'm hovering sits on it. also sort the pinned table by whichever property is selected, highest first
my pins are gone every time I reopen it. can it remember them, and which property I had on? and a button to clear them all
small one: in the pinned panel say where the element ranks for each property, like 5th highest of 51. I'm using this to explain to a student why Zn and Fe behave so differently
the radius rank for O says "51st highest of 54" which is a weird way to put it, say 4th lowest when its in the bottom half
